transcript: Bengaluru's AI traffic camera fined a man 500 rupees for carrying a guitar. Last week, a Bengaluru woman got a 500 rupees traffic fine on her phone. The offense was pillion riding without a helmet, but she was not on the scooter. Her husband was riding alone, wearing a helmet, with guitar on his back. To understand how a guitar got fined, you need to know how Bengaluru catches traffic offenses now. The city runs something called ITMS, the Intelligent Traffic Management System. Think of it as a network of 250 AI cameras spread across 50 big junctions. These are not normal CCTV cameras. They read your number plate the moment you pass, and they run an AI on the live video that has been trained to spot seven things: jumping a red light, crossing the stop line, no helmet, speeding, three people on a bike, phone in hand, no seat belt. No cop is needed. The camera sees it, the AI flags it. A team at the traffic management center is supposed to look at the photo and confirm it. Then, the system pulls your vehicle details, generates an e-challan, and you get an SMS with a link to the photo. A paper notice follows to your home. So what went wrong with the guitar? The AI saw a big black shape behind the rider, roughly the size of a person, nothing that looked like a helmet on top. To the machine, that was a second passenger. It flagged the violation, and the human check did not catch it either. The rider posted the photo on X and tagged the traffic police. They replied asking him to contact their automation section to get it cancelled. Now here is the honest part: this is not a one-off. Earlier this month, also in Karnataka, a car received a no helmet notice. A car. Police called it a technical glitch. The system is fast, it works 24 hours a day, and it catches thousands of real offenders. But the AI is guessing from a single photo, and the human who is meant to double check is looking at thousands of them. The AI does the watching. The human is still the last line of defense, and that line has holes. So next time an e-challan lands on your phone, open the photo before you pay. If you see a guitar being fined for a helmet, you know what to do. Have you ever got a challan that made no sense? Tell me in the comments. And I drop updates like this first in my free WhatsApp community. Link in bio.
